**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Thank you for the care in this change. The picks move to one operation-level field. Each path writes an undoable command, a serde-default project key and a digest. The trial merge with main is clean. The touched suites, clippy and the light lane are green.

### What looks good

- The stored pick goes through commands: `EditOperationParams` writes `params.picks` and sets `stamp: None`; its `invert` puts the previous operation back. The UI (`start_exit_rows.rs`, `start_exit_pick.rs`) writes the page draft only, and Apply rides `EditOperationParams`. `edit_sets_the_pick_and_undo_restores_the_automatic_seam` pins it (`crates/app/tests/contour_start_point.rs:97`).
- The project file is serde-default on every `ParamsDto` arm (`crates/app/src/project/params.rs`), so a file without `picks` loads the old behaviour. The legacy keys are read-only (`#[serde(default, skip_serializing)]` in `crates/app/src/project/approach.rs:79` and `crates/app/src/project/wire_edm_dto.rs`), and `with_legacy` moves them into `picks` (`crates/app/src/project/path_picks_dto.rs:76`). The two load tests pin this.
- **The regeneration guard holds. No stale toolpath can post after a pick change.** `stamp_picks` digests a start pick (`0xC7`) and an exit pick (`0xC8`) after `stamp_links` (`crates/app/src/operation/params/digest.rs:296`), and the wire start stays in `stamp_cutting` (`crates/app/src/operation/params/cutting.rs:51`). `current_stamp` reads both, so a changed pick moves the stamp. `EditOperationParams` sets `stamp: None` (`crates/app/src/commands/operation/edit.rs:181`), so `status_of` answers `Stale`. `posting::program_ops` refuses a `Stale` op: "inputs moved since generation - regenerate before posting" (`crates/app/src/posting.rs:867`). Undo restores the previous stamp with the previous pick, so the cache and the stored pick stay together. `the_stamp_tells_a_pick_apart` pins the digest (`crates/app/tests/contour_start_point.rs:127`).
- The pick's geometry is still refused by name, never moved. A pick farther than the reach from every ring is refused (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_start.rs:116`). A pick no band reaches is deferred and then refused (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_whole.rs:375`). A tilted contour, an open chain, control or wear compensation, tabs with a lead, keep-down and a stated overlap each refuse by name. `PathPicks::refusal()` bounds the coordinates and the count (`crates/motion/src/path_picks.rs:97`) and `ContourParams::validate` calls it, so a hand-edited degenerate pick refuses at generation.
- The MCP surface carries the change: `add_operation` and `edit_operation` take `picks`, and `migrate_legacy_patch` moves the old wire `start` and the old `links.approach.start_point` / `exit_point` into `picks` (`crates/app/src/project/path_picks_dto.rs:91`). `list_operation_types` reports `picks` and the `camcraft-mcp` skill row is updated. This PR adds no new command, so it needs no new MCP tool.
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in production code. The pick maths is clamped and checked. No golden file and no snapshot PNG changed.
- Process: the body says `Process change: yes`, the PR edits only `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`, and it does not touch `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`.

### Results (built locally, trial merge of head with origin/main `81365c33b`; the base is the same tree)

The trial merge with main is clean (no conflict). The PR author is a contributor, so I built locally and did not use the self-hosted runner. `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main --dry-run` maps the diff to about 340 suites, because the change adds `picks:` to test literals in nearly every app test file; that is not a sane quick plan, so I ran the pinning suites and the suites the change touches by name.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| Build `camcraft-motion` + `camcraft-app` test binaries | pass (exit 0) |
| `contour_start_point` | 10 passed |
| `start_exit_shared` | 4 passed |
| `wire_stamp` | 7 passed |
| `mcp_wire_contour` | 8 passed |
| `wire_contour` | 8 passed |
| `mcp_edit_machine` | 8 passed |
| `agie_native` | 33 passed |
| `cut_recipe` | 20 passed |
| `sketch_engrave_trace` | 12 passed |
| `project_roundtrip` | 84 passed |
| `golden_cl` | 34 passed |
| `camcraft-ui --lib` (full) | 1608 passed, 0 failed, 8 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` | pass, 0 warnings (one pre-existing unused workspace dependency warning, not from this PR) |
| Light lane (`cargo xtask gate light`, release) | pass: 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, wall 5.3 min |

### Targeted tests

- No post or toolpath output changed (the goldens are unchanged), so the example catalog suites are not owed. The `golden_cl` contour suite is green.
- Light lane (`cargo xtask gate light`): pass. Six steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled: light build, `motion light: lib`, `motion light: adaptive_troch_island`, `motion light: adaptive_troch_neck`, `motion light: adaptive_troch_parallel`, `app light: pocket_pass_start`.
- Heavy step: none. This is a `feat` `P2` PR, so it needs no targeted heavy step. It merges at the next cut.

### Requested before merge

None. The items below are notes, not blockers.

### Questions and notes (not blocking)

- **Project churn on load (documented).** A project saved with a contour start or exit pick reads `Stale` once after the update: on main the pick bytes were inside the `0xC3` approach block; here they come after the links block. The post refuses such an op until it is regenerated. The decision file and the `Changelog:` line say this. This is the trade the previous review allowed. If you want zero churn, write the old byte order for the kinds that have `links` and pin a stamp value that main computed.
- **Tool text vs merge patch.** The `edit_operation` description says "null or {} clears" (`crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs`). In an RFC 7386 merge an empty object is a no-op, so `picks: {}` does not clear an existing pick. `picks: null` or `picks: { start: [], exit: [] }` does. Consider "null or empty role lists clear".
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill still lists `start` among the wire Contour "All fields". `list_operation_types` now reports `picks`; `start` is accepted as a legacy key only. A one-word tidy.
- The commits end `Refs #3339`; the PR body ends `Fixes #3339`, so the issue closes on merge. This is fine; `Fixes` in the commit body would match the letter of the law.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

Thank you for the refresh. This is a delta review of the new head. The conflict resolution is correct. Both sides are present. Nothing from main is lost.

### Refresh class: DELTA

`cargo xtask merge-plan --delta 3871 --reviewed f753cd46e` prints DELTA. The only hand edit is in `crates/app/src/operation/agie_profile.rs`. The remerge-diff of `f46d8fb9a` shows that file only.

### The conflict resolution

The automatic merge clashed in `agie_sketch_job`. Your resolution keeps both sides:

- Your side keeps the picks: `wire.picks.first(PickRole::Start)` and `let start = [start.xy.x, start.xy.y]` (`crates/app/src/operation/agie_profile.rs:79-83`).
- Main's side keeps the new wire profile: `chain.wire_profile()`, `shape.bounds()` and `shape.place()` (`:84`, `:91`, `:95`).

The other two pick sites keep your side: `agie_job` at `:52` and `checked` at `:149` and `:152`. The file has no conflict marks, no `wire.start` and no `round_profile()` call. The diff of the head against `origin/main` `02d05bc1c` holds only the three pick substitutions.

### What looks good

- The tree is whole. `origin/main` is `02d05bc1c`, the second parent of the merge. The trial merge is a fast-forward.
- `Process change: yes` is in the body. The only process file is `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`. The PR does not edit `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`.
- The body ends `Fixes #3339`. Issue #3339 is open, and the change does what it asks.
- The PR adds no user-facing command, so it needs no new MCP tool. It extends `add_operation` and `edit_operation` with `picks`.
- The resolved file has no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!`. No golden file and no snapshot PNG changed.

### Results (built locally, worktree `review/3871d-delta`, tree f46d8fb9a)

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --no-run` | pass (exit 0) |
| `agie_native` | 36 passed, 0 failed |
| `contour_start_point` | 10 passed, 0 failed |
| `wire_contour` | 8 passed, 0 failed |
| `wire_stamp` | 7 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | pass, 0 errors (one pre-existing workspace manifest warning) |
| Light lane (`cargo xtask gate light`) | pass: 6 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, wall 6.0 min |

The quick dry-run maps this 589-file diff to 816 steps, which is not a sane plan. So I ran the suites that cover the resolved file and your pinning tests by name.

### Targeted tests

- `agie_native` covers the resolved `agie_sketch_job` and `agie_job`. It is green.
- Light lane row: light build (43 s), `motion light: lib` (257 s), `motion light: adaptive_troch_island` (34 s), `motion light: adaptive_troch_neck` (14 s), `motion light: adaptive_troch_parallel` (8 s), `app light: pocket_pass_start` (2 s). 0 failed.
- No post or toolpath golden changed, so the example catalog suites are not owed.
- Heavy step: none. This is a `feat` `P2` PR. It merges at the next cut.

### Requested before merge

None.

### Questions and notes (not blocking)

- This is a `feat` PR. It merges at the next cut, not now.
- The earlier notes still stand: the one-time regeneration after update, and that `picks: {}` does not clear a pick. They are not new findings.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
